clue.text: Statement suggesting cleric's 'competence not cast in stone?

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a clergyman
the 's is read as the contraction of 'is'
having competence means being able; the statement is that the cleric is able

explanation.surface: A remark praising a clergyman's ability is somehow not fixed for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening words describe the statement 'Rev is able', which spelt as one word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not cast in stone is open to change, so it can be revised or amended later.

clue.text: Puzzle about one of three coming in quick succession?

parts.note: re means about or concerning

parts.words: one of three coming in quick succession
parts.note: the joke that you wait ages for a bus and then three come at once

explanation.surface: A puzzle about why buses always arrive in threes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle that uses pictures or symbols to represent words.

clue.text: From harvest I get what's left over

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: From the harvest I collect whatever remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestige is a trace or remnant of something that has otherwise gone.

clue.text: Desk terrible muddle? Bunk off quickly!

indicators.note: terrible says the desk's letters are in a mess, needing rearrangement

parts.note: to addle is to muddle or confuse

explanation.surface: A terribly muddled desk prompts someone to slip away fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges DESK into SKED. 'Bunk off' is British for skiving off, leaving when you should be working.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is to run off hastily, the same as to bunk off quickly.

clue.text: In terrible state, king has little energy for pudding

indicators.note: king and energy go in the word for terrible

parts.note: terrible means bad
K is the chess abbreviation for king
E, a little piece, is the abbreviation for energy
Alaska is a US state

explanation.surface: Stuck in an awful condition, a king has little energy left for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Baked Alaska is a dessert of ice cream and sponge covered with meringue and browned.

clue.text: Beginning of boom: be over decline

indicators.note: over says the word be is turned round
only the first letter of boom is used

explanation.surface: At the start of a boom, prepare for a decline.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' turns BE into EB; 'boom' looks like the economy taking off, which sets up the contrasting decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To ebb is to decline or recede, as the tide does.

clue.text: Remove problem from hopeful girl once: unattractive front half

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, was a young woman making her hopeful entrance into society

indicators.note: only the front half of the word for unattractive is kept, its first two letters

parts.note: unattractive means ugly

explanation.surface: A one-time debutante is told that the front half of her face is unattractive.
explanation.definitionFit: To debug is to locate and remove faults, especially errors in computer software.

clue.text: A hurt daughter set up a histrionic situation

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the pieces are written upwards, reversed

parts.note: to mar is to hurt or spoil

explanation.surface: A hurt daughter stages a scene of theatrical emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: A + MAR + D read upwards gives DRAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is an exciting or emotional situation, as in 'making a drama' of something.

clue.text: Bloke participating in match? May he win!

definitions.text: Bloke participating in match? May he win!

parts.words: Bloke participating in match? May he win!
parts.note: the match is a wedding, and the phrase 'may the ... win' completes the saying

explanation.surface: A sporting contestant is wished good luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Match looks sporting, but it is a marriage; the wedding attendant also appears in the saying 'may the best man win'.
explanation.definitionFit: The best man is the groom's chief attendant at a wedding, a match.

clue.text: Engelbert developed land he shouldn't have?

indicators.note: developed says the letters of the name are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A man called Engelbert built on land where he had no right to build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges ENGELBERT, and also finishes the definition: land he shouldn't have developed.
explanation.definitionFit: Green belt is protected countryside round a town where building development is restricted.

clue.text: Bear witness to magistrate having hidden sixth sense?

indicators.note: the magistrate holds the sixth sense concealed within him, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: beak is British slang for a magistrate or judge
ESP, extrasensory perception, is the so-called sixth sense

explanation.surface: A magistrate may have a hidden sixth sense when hearing witnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: To bespeak is to be evidence of or indicate something, as a witness testifies to it.

clue.text: Club that is going after money

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'that is' follows the money in the answer

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A club, which means someone is chasing cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A brassie is an old name for a wooden golf club, the number two wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassie is a golf club, a wooden club once soled with brass.

clue.text: Star with sex appeal —— picture to be framed

indicators.note: the picture is put in a frame formed by the other piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: A sexy film star's photograph is about to be framed.
explanation.definitionFit: Spica is the brightest star in the constellation Virgo, an actual named star.

clue.text: Pets needing endless fruit and fish

parts.note: dogs are pets

indicators.note: the fruit loses its final letter

parts.note: an almond is a fruit (a nut, botanically a drupe)

explanation.surface: Pet animals need a diet of fruit and fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog salmon, or chum salmon, is a Pacific species of salmon, so a fish.

clue.text: Swap seen as compromise

definitions.meaning: an exchange where each side gives and receives
mutual concession where each side yields something

explanation.surface: An exchange is regarded as a form of compromise.
explanation.definitionFit: Give and take means both a mutual exchange and willingness to make concessions.

clue.text: Run, offering word of farewell

definitions.meaning: in cricket a ... is a run scored from a ball that passes the batsman without being hit

explanation.surface: Someone leaves at a run, calling goodbye over their shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a cricket run not off the bat, and the casual parting word.

clue.text: County gives stupid people money for services maybe

parts.note: berk is British slang for a fool
hire is payment for the use of something or someone's services

explanation.surface: A county pays foolish people for their services.
explanation.walkthrough: BERKSHIRE is an English county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Berkshire is an English county, the Royal County lying west of London.

clue.text: Formal utterance to condemn twisting during waltz?

indicators.note: the twisted word comes in the middle of the dance

parts.note: a waltz is an example of a dance

indicators.note: twisting tells us to turn the word for condemn round, read backwards

parts.note: to revile is to condemn or denounce

explanation.surface: A formal speech condemns the way someone twists during a waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' makes ELIVER, sitting inside the dance; the question mark warns that a waltz is only one example of the dance needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliverance is a formal pronouncement or verdict, such as a judge's considered statement.

clue.text: Trustworthy agent, acceptable to top people, put on the board

parts.note: a rep, representative, is an agent
U means upper-class, acceptable in the best circles
to table a motion is to put it before a committee or board

explanation.surface: An agent, accepted by the elite, is made a board member.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputable means having a good reputation, so trusted and trustworthy.

clue.text: Perhaps masseuses thank politician for giving endorsement!

parts.note: masseuses rub people, so they are examples of rubbers
ta is British informal for thank you
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: Masseuses thank a politician for endorsing them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber stamp is an automatic approval given without proper scrutiny, an endorsement.

clue.text: Measure of living organisms, including fish round island

indicators.note: the fish goes round the island, enclosing it

parts.note: the bass is a fish
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man, an island

explanation.surface: Counting the living things includes fish around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' only joins the definition to the wordplay; the island is the Isle of Man, whose standard abbreviation solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Biomass is the total mass of living organisms in a given area.

clue.text: Wounded? Stop shooting!

definitions.meaning: someone ... has been wounded by a blade
'...!' is the film director's call to stop the cameras rolling

explanation.surface: A gunfight victim cries out for the shooting to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut means wounded, and it is also the director's order to halt filming.

clue.text: Tory type as helpmate

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory
a sort is a type or kind

explanation.surface: A Conservative type of person as a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a spouse or companion, a helpmate to a partner.

clue.text: What secretary uses for making notes — but it's not for the minutes!

definitions.text: What secretary uses for making notes
definitions.meaning: secretaries take dictation in a rapid abbreviated script
on a clock the ... marks the hours, not the minutes

explanation.surface: A secretary's note-taking script is, oddly, unsuitable for writing up the minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: Minutes look like a meeting's record, but they are the minutes on a clock face; split the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand is the rapid writing system secretaries use, and a clock's short hand shows hours.

clue.text: Excursion not quiet — notice three making a sound?

indicators.note: not says the quiet letter is taken out of the excursion

parts.note: a trip is an excursion
P, piano, means quiet in music
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A noisy outing with an advert about three musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a three-note chord, three notes sounded together.

clue.text: Capital garments -—- you won't get cold

indicators.note: the cold is not present, so its letter is taken away from the garments

parts.note: tunics are garments
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Wearing these garments, you won't catch cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia.

clue.text: Monks ultimately accept vow

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of monks

parts.note: to wear something is to accept or tolerate it

explanation.surface: Monks finally take a vow.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to vow or make a solemn promise.

clue.text: Sort of poet with aim possibly to get to the heart

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of 'aim' may be arranged another way

parts.note: the gist of something is its heart or essence

explanation.surface: A poet aims to get to the heart of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles the three letters to IMA; 'Sort of poet' signals a school of poets rather than a general word for a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: An imagist was a poet of the early twentieth-century Imagism movement, favouring clear precise imagery.

clue.text: Bath has raised an objection

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone raised an objection to the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is a bath, as in a bathtub.

clue.text: A bishop got out of bed after appearance of a doctor

indicators.note: the word for getting up comes after the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
rose means got up out of bed

explanation.surface: A bishop gets up once a doctor has appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Ambrose was the fourth-century Bishop of Milan, so he was a bishop.

clue.text: Freed from pain, stopped losing head

indicators.note: the word for stopped loses its first letter

parts.note: ceased means stopped

explanation.surface: Someone's pain stopped once they lost their head.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain that has been eased is relieved, so the sufferer is freed from it.

clue.text: Worker perhaps undertaking to accompany the Queen?

definitions.text: Worker perhaps undertaking to accompany the Queen?

parts.note: a worker bee is one example of a bee
a feat is a notable undertaking or achievement
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone promises to act as an escort to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accompany' is a link: the pieces simply sit side by side. Beefeaters are the Yeomen Warders of the Tower of London, royal guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeaters are the royal bodyguard, Yeomen who attend the sovereign on ceremonial occasions.
